In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have shown that the semi-online model can be used for a variety of geometric problems, but it is a rather weak model for many of the most basic problems.
the semi-online maintenance model is a powerful tool to obtain nontrivial results in dynamic geometric optimization and measure computation.
the semi-online model is a useful and interesting model for dynamic optimization, but that the problems that can be solved in sublinear time in it are not as numerous as one might have expected.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that for most basic geometric optimization problems, the online and offline models differ in their worst-case behavior.
we can solve most of the basic geometric problems in constant amortized time per update, with the exception of the convex hull problem, which can be solved with O(log n) update time.

we can handle the dynamic Hausdorff problem and the dynamic discrete 1-center problem fully dynamically, while for the other problems we can handle the semi-online versions with update time sublinear in n.
The main takeaway from our work is that
semi-online geometric problems can be much easier than fully-online ones.
semi-online algorithms can be surprisingly powerful.

, in the semi-online model and for geometric problems, the time needed for the insertion and deletion of an object is not the main factor, but rather the time to compute a new optimal solution after the deletion of an object.
